rows.title_full: AN ACT ESTABLISHING A RENTAL HOUSING SUBSIDY PROGRAM FOR INFORMAL SETTLER FAMILIES AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR
rows.title_short: Rental Housing Subsidy Program Act
rows.abstract:
Aims to provide informal settler families (ISFs) access to the formal housing market as an option to address the temporary relocation of displaced families due to natural and man-made disasters.
Allocates a flat rental subsidy rate of Three Thousand Five Hundred Pesos (P3,000.00) for those living in Metro Manila and a rental subsidy rate to be determined by the DHSUD and the NEDA for those living in all other regions provided the rental subsidy shall not exceed the actual rent.
Grants the rental subsidy to eligible beneficiaries until the date of completion of the permanent housing project intended for them or upon their actual transfer to the permanent housing project, whichever comes first.
rows.status: Approved by the House on 2023-12-12, transmitted to the Senate on 2023-12-13 and received by the Senate on 2023-12-13

rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING ADDITIONAL CRITERION FOR THE AVAILMENT OF THE UNPROGRAMMED APPROPRIATIONS, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE REPUBLIC ACT NO. 11936 OR THE 2023 GENERAL APPROPRIATIONS ACT
rows.title_short: Providing Additional Criterion For The Availment Of The Unprogrammed Appropriations, Amending For The Purpose Republic Act No. 11936 Or The 2023 General Appropriations Act
rows.abstract:
Aims to maximize the idle funds of the GOCCs and further help the national government´s requirements and fund the much needed unprogrammed projects.
Seeks to amend Section 1 of the Special Provision of the Unprogrammed Appropriations of R.A. No. 11936 or the FY 2023 General Appropriations Act to read as follows:
“Special Provision(s)
1.	Availment of the Unprogrammed Appropriations. The amounts authorized herein for Purpose Nos. 1-2, 4-7 and 9-61 may be used when any of the following exists:
(a)	Excess revenue collections in any [one of the identified] TAX OR non-tax revenue sources from its corresponding revenue collection target, as reflected in the BESF;
(b)	New revenue collection or those arising from new tax or non-tax sources which are not part of, nor included in, the original revenue sources reflected in the BESF; [or]
(c)	Approved loans for foreign-assisted projects[.]; OR
(D)  FUNDS OF GOVERNMENT -OWNED OR -CONTROLLED CORPORATIONS DETERMINED TO BE IN EXCESS OF THEIR CURRENT ADMINISTRATIVES AND OPERATIONS EXPENSES, BENEFIT OBLIGATIONS, OR RESERVE REQUIREMENTS.”
rows.status: Approved by the House on 2023-11-29, transmitted to the Senate on 2023-12-06 and received by the Senate on 2023-12-06

rows.author: H057;
rows.title_full: AN ACT TO AMEND THE PARTNERSHIP PROVISIONS OF THE NEW CIVIL CODE
rows.abstract:
Seeks to exclude corporations from participation as partners within the classical partnership framework outlined in the Civil Code.
Proposes to enjoins corporations to establish joint ventures guided by the prevailing corporate laws or general contract law to clarify the legal landscape and promote greater legal clarity and consistency.
Proposes to amend Art.1767 of Republic Act No. 386, which partly read as follows:
“Corporations shall not be eligible to form a partnership under Title IX; however, corporations may be allowed to form contractual or corporate joint ventures . . .”
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on REVISION OF LAWS since 2023-11-15

rows.title_full: AN ACT TO AMEND GENERAL BANKING LAW OF 2000 TO PROVIDE THE STANDARD OF DILIGENCE OF BANKS
rows.abstract:
States that the standard of diligence for banks shall be intermediate diligence, which means the degree of diligence that is “more than the diligence of a good father of a family but less than extraordinary diligence.

Proposes to amend Sec.6 of Republic Act No.8791 to describe the standard of diligence required of banks; Tasks the Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas in providing additional guidelines pertaining to intermediate diligence.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on BANKS AND FINANCIAL INTERMEDIARIES since 2023-11-15

rows.author: F008;
rows.title_full: AN ACT CREATING THE PHILIPPINE RENEWABLE ENERGY CORPORATION, DEFINING ITS POWERS AND FUNCTIONS, AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR
rows.abstract:
Refers the term RE resources to energy resources that do not have an upper limit on the total quantity to be used . . .These include, among others, biomass, solar, wind, geothermal, ocean energy, and hydropower, with internationally accepted norms and standards on dams, and other emerging RE technologies.
Provides that the Corporation shall promote and undertake research development, . . . and commercial application of new, renewable, non-conventional, and environmental-friendly energy sources and other natural, non-fossil fuel . . .
Proposes to abolish the PNOC-Renewables Corporation (PNOC-RC);  to exclude the Agus and Pulangui Hydroelectric Power Plant Complexes and other hydroelectric facilities from among generation assets that will be privatized, pursuant to the Electric Power Industry Reform Act (EPIRA), their ownership shall be transferred to and operated by the Corporation . . .

rows.title_full: AN ACT ACCORDING EQUAL RIGHTS TO WIVES AND HUSBANDS IN THE PHILIPPINES BY AMENDING ARTICLE 333, 334, AND 344 OF THE REVISED PENAL CODE
rows.abstract:
Seeks to do away with gender-based discrimination by punishing acts of marital infidelity committed by either spouse.
Provides that adultery and concubinage shall thereafter be sexual infidelity and maintaining a paramour, respectively.
States that “ `PARAMOUR´ SHALL INCLUDE ANY PERSON WHO COHABITS WITH A MARRIED  PERSON UNDER CIRCUMSTANCES WHERE THEY ASSUME AND EXERCISE TOWARD EACH OTHER THE RIGHTS AND PRIVILEGES WHICH PROPERLY BELONG TO PERSONS MARRIED TO EACH OTHER.

rows.title_full: AN ACT AMENDING PRESIDENTIAL DECREE NO. 1621, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE "ANTI-FENCING LAW"
rows.abstract:
Seeks to address the non-concomitant adjustment of the penalties provided under PD 1612 upon the enactment of RA 10951 (AN ACT ADJUSTING THE AMOUNT OR THE VALUE OF PROPERTY AND DAMAGE ON WHICH A PENALTY IS BASED, AND THE FINES IMPOSED UNDER THE REVISED PENAL CODE, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE ACT NO. 3815, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS “THE REVISED PENAL CODE”, AS AMENDED).
Proposes that the penalties for fencing be adjusted based on the penalties for theft and robbery under RA 10951 (since fencing is an accessory crime of Theft and Robbery) with a corresponding penalty based on the value or amount of the property taken by the offender.

rows.title_full: AN ACT PROTECTING GOOD SAMARITANS WHO PROVIDE ASSISTANCE TO THOSE IN NEED
rows.abstract:
Defines the term “Good Samaritan” as an individual who voluntarily and in good faith provides reasonable assistance to another person in need of emergency care, assistance, or aid.
Intends to establish legal safeguards and protection from liability for any unintentional harm that may occur due to the Good Samaritan´s action.
Proposes that immunity from liability shall extend to actions such as administering first aid, cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR), using an automated external defibrillator (AED), or any other reasonable assistance expected to a person with similar training and experience.

rows.title_short: Chemical Weapons Prohibition Act
rows.abstract:
Seeks to prohibit the State and all persons from developing, producing, manufacturing, acquiring, possessing, stockpiling, retaining, or using chemical weapons or engaging in any other activities prohibited under the Chemical Weapons Convention. 
Designates the Anti-Terrorism Council (ATC) as the Philippine National Authority on Chemical Weapons Convention (PNA-CWC), to be headed by the Executive Secretary as Chairperson.
Provides penalties and sanctions for any person who violates this Act. In case the violation is committed by any partnership, corporation, association or juridical entity, the registration and license to operate shall be cancelled and revoked permanently and will be held criminally liable.
Mandates the PNA-CWC to forfeit any chemical weapon found anywhere in the territory or in any other place under the jurisdiction of the Philippines to be destroyed or disposed of in accordance with existing environmental regulations or related applicable laws.
Provides the mechanisms for the declaration, verification and inspection of toxic chemicals and their precursors.

rows.author: K077;
rows.title_full:
AN ACT AMENDING ARTICLE 2180 OF REPUBLIC ACT NO. 386, OTHERWISE KNOWN
AS THE CIVIL CODE OF THE PHILIPPINES, TO INCLUDE ACADEMIC EDUCATIONAL
INSTITUTIONS
rows.abstract:
Seeks to amend article 2180 of the Civil Code to read as follows:
“Article 2180. The obligation imposed by article 2176 is demandable not only for one´s own acts or omissions, but also for those of persons for whom one is responsible . . .
Lastly, teachers or heads of establishments of arts and trades OR ACADEMIC EDUCATIONAL INSTITUTIONS shall be liable for damages caused by their pupils and students or apprentices, so long as they remain in their custody . . .”.
Note:  “Article 2176. Whoever by act or omission causes damage to another, there being fault or negligence, is obliged to pay for the damage done”.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on REVISION OF LAWS since 2023-11-28

rows.author: K077;
rows.title_full:
AN ACT ADJUSTING THE MINIMUM AMOUNT FOR DEATH INDEMNITY, MORAL AND
EXEMPLARY DAMAGES UNDER REPUBLIC ACT NO. 386 OR THE CIVIL CODE OF THE
PHILIPPINES
rows.abstract:
Amends Article 2206 of the Civil Code to read as follows;
“Art. 2206. 
The amount of damages for death caused by a crime or quasi-delict SHALL BE AT LEAST THREE HUNDRED THOUSAND PESOS, even though there may have been mitigating circumstances. THE COURT, IN ITS DISCRETION, MAY AWARD A HIGHER AMOUNT, BASED ON THE RATE OF INFLATION AND THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF EACH CASE, . . ."
Amends Article 2216 of the same Act to read as follows:
“Article 2216.  No proof of pecuniary loss is necessary in order that moral, nominal, temperate, liquidated or exemplary damages, may be adjudicated.  The assessment of such damages . . . PROVIDED, THAT THE AMOUNT OF MORAL AND EXEMPLARY DAMAGES SHALL BE AT LEAST TWO HUNDRED THOUSAND PESOS IN CASE OF DEATH RESULTING FROM A CRIME OR QUASI-DELICT.  THE COURT, IN ITS DISCRETION, MAY AWARD A HIGHER AMOUNT BASED ON PREVAILING CIRCUMSTANCES AND THE RATE OF INFLATION.”
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on REVISION OF LAWS since 2023-11-28

rows.author: K077;
rows.title_full: AN ACT REQUIRING EMPLOYERS TO INFORM THEIR EMPLOYEES OF THEIR RIGHTS, BENEFITS AND PRIVILEGES UNDER EXISTING LAWS, AND COMPANY POLICIES OR EMPLOYMENT CONTRACTS
rows.abstract:
Proposes to put in place a mechanism for employers to inform their new hires and present employees about their rights and benefits under the law.
Seeks to grant the Department of Labor and Employment the authority to create educational modules about fundamental labor rights and to enforce stringent monitoring measures to ensure employers´ compliance.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on LABOR AND EMPLOYMENT since 2023-11-28

rows.author: K077;
rows.title_full:
AN ACT MANDATING SALARY OFFER TRANSPARENCY IN JOB ADVERTISEMENTS,
PROHIBITING INQUIRY ON EMPLOYEE´S SALARY HISTORY, PROVIDING PENALTIES
THEREFOR, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract:
Aims to address the issue of wage inequality and promote more equitable and just compensation practices.
Mandates covered employers, particularly private entities with ten or more employees, to disclose the minimum and maximum salary ranges for advertised job positions, promotions, or transfer opportunities.
Seeks to ensure transparency in salary offers, prevent discrimination, and promote equality in employment opportunities.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on LABOR AND EMPLOYMENT since 2023-11-28
